findings.title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results via positional zip
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that typically only contains entries for nodes that were actually found (missing/expired nodes are simply absent). The code then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` to pair each error_id with its fetched data. If any single error_id's node is missing from nodestore, `events` will have fewer entries than `error_ids`, and zip() pairs the remaining items positionally rather than by key — causing every subsequent error_id to be paired with the wrong event's title/message. The fix is to look up each error_id's data by its generated node_id (e.g. `events.get(node_id)`), not rely on positional correspondence.

findings.title: Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared against breadcrumb timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: In gen_request_data, `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` compares the error event's timestamp (sourced from the Sentry Event model via fetch_error_details, which is a float number of seconds since epoch) directly against the breadcrumb/rrweb event's `timestamp` field, which for recording segment events is conventionally milliseconds since epoch. Because these two values differ in scale by a factor of ~1000, the chronological interleaving logic will be wrong in production: error timestamps (~1e9) will almost always appear smaller than breadcrumb timestamps (~1e12), so errors will be emitted far earlier in the generated log than they actually occurred. The included tests use artificially small, homogeneous-unit timestamps for both error and breadcrumb events, which hides this unit mismatch.

findings.title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references PRCommentWorkflow instead of the defining class
findings.body: The new `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` static method is added to `CommitContextIntegration`, and it calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` rather than calling the sibling static method on the class it's actually defined in. `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Unless `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`, this cross-class reference will raise an AttributeError at runtime when GitHub/GitLab's `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` (both subclasses of `PRCommentWorkflow`) call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` to build suspect-issue PR comments, which would break that comment feature entirely. Even if it happens to resolve today, it is a fragile, incorrect reference that should use the class itself (e.g. `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title` or just `_truncate_title`) rather than an unrelated class name.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty data behind a feature flag
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the table widget now renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with hardcoded empty arrays instead of passing through the actual `eventView`/`result.data` that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch uses. Any organization with this flag enabled will see an always-empty table regardless of the underlying query results, which is a functional regression/incomplete wiring if the flag is or becomes active.

findings.title: Undocumented default behavior change for autofix automation tuning
findings.body: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT is changed from "low" to "off" (mirrored in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py), meaning Seer Autofix will no longer run automatically by default for projects that rely on the default. This is a meaningful behavior change affecting all projects without an explicit setting, but it's unrelated to the stated PR title/description ("Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System" / "Test 5") and has no explanation, making it hard for reviewers to assess intent or impact.
